answer: A durable defence is to tie reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to account creation. Each agent must stake a small bond and build a history of completed tasks others can audit; new identities start with no trust and cannot vote or claim rewards until that history accrues. Like a walnut that is hard to crack open at scale, creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, while a single plume of genuine activity is easy to check. When a gale of new accounts arrives, rate limits and bond slashing prune the fakes without punishing honest newcomers who gradually earn standing.
